name: Tehran Persian (Standard Iranian)

ancestors.notes: New Persian descent; Tehran dialect became standard ~19th c.
Arabic adstrate: 40–50% of formal vocabulary; consonants θ/ð/ħ/ʕ/q assimilated phonologically

notes: Tehran Standard Persian — the national standard of Iran. DEFINING VOWEL SHIFT (vs. Classical/Dari/Tajik): Classical ā [aː] → Tehran [ɒː] (backed); Classical a → [æ] (fronted). 6-VOWEL SYSTEM: ɒː, æ, e, o, iː, uː (no contrastive length). Voiceless stops aspirated [pʰ tʰ kʰ] in onset. q/ɣ merger: Arabic ق and غ both → [ɣ] or [ɢ]. ħ → h (pharyngeal lost); ʕ → ʔ (often deleted). r → [ɾ] tap in most positions. COLLOQUIAL LAYER (vs. the fa formal standard this spec bases on): word-final -ān is commonly raised to [-uːn] in casual/colloquial speech (nān 'bread' -> [nuːn], jān 'dear/soul' -> [dʒuːn]; Jahangiri 2000; Windfuhr 2009). ENGINE LIMIT: the raising is conditioned on word-final position of the -ān sequence specifically (not all ɒː), which this phoneme-level allophone map cannot express positionally since ا and ن are separate graphemes; [uː] is listed as an available conditioned variant of ɒː rather than a positionally-triggered rule. A second colloquial reduction (frequent function/adverb words in -ar losing the rhotic and lowering, e.g. digar 'other' -> dige, agar 'if' -> age) is lexically restricted to a closed set of high-frequency words rather than a general phonological rule, so it is documented here but intentionally NOT encoded as a grapheme/allophone override (would overgeneralize to unrelated -ar words, e.g. bāzār 'market').
